You're wrong; "Achiles's heel" (and "Jesus' name") are exceptions to the general rule.  See [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style#Possessives]: "For the possessive of singular nouns, including proper names and words ending in s, add 's (my daughter's achievement, my niece's wedding, Cortez's men, the boss's office, Illinois's largest employer, Descartes's philosophy, Verreaux's eagle)."  Remember, always look to the WP Manual of Style, not the AP Stylebook.

Undid revision 1077319055 by [[Special:Contributions/AuH2ORepublican|AuH2ORepublican]] ([[User talk:AuH2ORepublican|talk]]) According to AP style it's correct to remove the s after apostrophe. [[Achilles' heel]] may be the most common example I can give.

Correcting orthography.  In English, an apostrophe-s is added to create a possessive, except when it is the possessive of a plural noun ending in "s," in which case only an apostrophe is added.  For example, one would write "Tom Jones's bicycle" (because "Jones" is a singular noun) but "the Joneses' babysitter" (because "Joneses" is a plural noun).  Likewise, it is spelled "Aaron Rodgers's uniform number" but, if one is talking about, say, his family growing up, "the Rodgerses' new home."
